title: Increment one counter under an async lock from eight tasks that yield inside it
summary: Eight async tasks on one thread each lock one shared async mutex, read a counter, yield once, write it back plus one and unlock, 500 to 2,000 times each, and the operation returns the final counter and the sum of all tickets.
notes: An asynchronous task on one thread: eight tasks contend for one async lock and each yields once while holding it, so every acquisition but the first of a turn has to suspend, queue and be woken. The figure is the lock's acquire, release and wake-up plus the runtime's scheduling of the yields and the waiting tasks; the yield is the same cheapest yield in every language. Each operation creates the lock and starts its eight tasks; starting them is part of the figure. No timer or sleep with a real delay is involved. Go runs with GOMAXPROCS=1, Rust on a single-thread executor, Python on one asyncio loop.
